These rows tested the same-window weekly credit model that #703 and #707 introduced and that shipped in 1.106.0. Under that model a week in which Anthropic reset the counter was reported as one row per calendar week, with the credit recorded in place and the week never re-anchored. The operator ruled that model incorrect: a reset ends one billing cycle and begins the next, and `cctally weekly` must show one row per billing cycle. Both features are reverted on this branch, so the behavior these rows assert no longer exists and the rows were removed with the code rather than retained against absent behavior. The pre-#703 tests covering cycle-anchored weeks are restored by the same revert and are live in this estate.

declarations.reason: These rows tested the dashboard Weekly panel's presentation-layer pre-credit synthesis ("Bug K") and the module-level segment cache that fed it: `BugKSegment`, `_bugk_key`, `cached_bugk_segment`, `reset_bugk_segment_state` and `reconcile_bugk_cache`. That synthesis existed because `_apply_reset_events_to_subweeks` did not split a week credited in place, so the dashboard rebuilt the missing pre-credit segment itself from its own `MIN(week_start_at)` query and its own re-fold. The applier now performs the split, which is where its twin `_apply_reset_events_to_weekrefs` has always performed it, so the credited week arrives as two ordinary SubWeek segments and the presentation-layer copy had to go in the same change: running both renders a credited week as three rows and double-counts the pre-credit cost. The code these rows exercise no longer exists. The three real-builder parity rows carried three different properties, and the replacement carries one of them. `test_bugk_segment_cache_parity` asserted that a closed pre-credit aggregate is served identically from cache and from scratch; `tests/test_dashboard_rebuild_parity.py::test_credited_week_group_a_cache_parity` carries exactly that, asserting byte-equality across cache-off, cold and warm over the same in-place-credit fixture. It does NOT carry the other two. `test_bugk_segment_cache_warm_no_refetch` asserted that a warm read does not re-fetch the closed pre-credit window, and `test_bugk_segment_cache_late_ingest_recomputes` asserted that a late ingest into that window evicts the entry and recomputes it. Neither property is specific to a credited week any more, because the Group A cache now owns the segment like any other week, so both are covered generically by the Group A suite in the same module rather than by a credit-specific row.

A rename, not a retirement. `test_subweek_and_weekref_appliers_agree_on_in_place_credit` seeded only the in-place-credit `week_reset_events` row shape, while `docs/credit-gotchas.md` described it as the tie that every change to either applier's case handling must go through. The test is now `test_subweek_and_weekref_appliers_agree_on_every_event_shape`, parametrized over all three shapes the two appliers handle — in-place credit, pre-reset truncation and post-reset shift — plus two spelling variants of the credit case. The former single case survives verbatim as the `in_place_credit` parameter, so the estate's added rows carry every assertion this row carried and four cases it did not. One of those additions found a real divergence: with the event row written in a non-UTC offset, `_apply_reset_events_to_weekrefs` matched raw column text and recognized nothing where `_apply_reset_events_to_subweeks` matched parsed instants and split the week.

The two `test_live_ingest_acquires_maintenance_before_ingest_lock` items carry the stats epoch in their parameter ids, so bumping `STATS_INDEX_EPOCH` from 1011 to 1012 renamed `[0-1011]` to `[0-1012]` and `[1011-1011]` to `[1012-1012]`. The test itself is unchanged. Coverage is preserved in every case: five rows leave and five equivalent rows arrive.

#750 S3's Unit A review withdrew the unestablished pre-credit echo guard, so the module that pinned it is renamed and rewritten. The guard reused an existing event when the predecessor reading exceeded the epoch maximum, but that maximum was computed over a window excluding the predecessor, so the condition held for any monotonically climbing series whose top value was observed exactly once -- an ordinary shape. A week credited at 63, observed climbing back to 63 and genuinely credited again lost its second credit. Deduplication is now exact-origin only, enforced by the epoch-1012 partial unique index, so these nine rows in tests/test_pre_credit_echo_guard.py name a mechanism that no longer exists and the module is tests/test_exact_origin_credit_dedup.py. Their successors: the reuse case becomes test_a5_a_climb_back_to_the_credited_level_is_credited_again pinning the counterexample series; the suppressed residual and the production echo sequence collapse into test_a5_a_stale_pre_credit_high_is_admitted_and_names_the_residual, because under the amended spec both are admitted and the two old cases seeded byte-identical data; the four controls are replaced by test_a5_a_replayed_observation_writes_exactly_one_event, test_a5_two_origins_both_write_on_one_legacy_boundary_tuple, test_a5_one_origin_under_two_accounts_writes_two_events and test_a5_two_origin_null_credits_on_one_tuple_write_one_event, which assert the identity that now decides rather than a series shape -- control D in particular passed for the wrong reason, ending its second climb at 58 against a pre-credit level of 63 so the 1pp band alone admitted it, and it duplicated control B; the account-scoping case becomes the one-origin-two-accounts case; and the pivots case becomes test_a5_the_pivots_run_on_the_credits_own_terms, driving a refused insert through the origin index instead of an echo reuse. One successor claim in the original text was WRONG and is corrected here. test_a5_the_recovery_delete_survives_a_rebuild_from_the_journal was declared to be succeeded by test_a5_a_delete_no_new_event_carries_is_journalled_as_its_own_effect, test_a5_a_winning_insert_emits_no_separate_recovery_event and test_a5_two_credits_in_one_week_survive_a_rebuild_as_two_events, and none of the three discharges it: the first two assert the recovery event's presence and its absence, which an inline DELETE satisfies equally, and the third rebuilds but wins both of its inserts, so it never reaches the refused-insert path. Acceptance criterion 4 was therefore undischarged for one commit. The review of this pass found that, and the following commit restores a case of the same name in tests/test_exact_origin_credit_dedup.py which rebuilds AFTER a refused insert and fails when the DELETE is inline. That successor arrived in a later transition than this declaration covers, so these rows stay retired rather than becoming renames.

The same transition as the retired echo-guard rows, reclassified. tests/test_in_place_credit_detection.py::test_dedup_via_the_echo_guard became test_a_replayed_pre_credit_high_is_admitted_as_its_own_event in the same file, on the same seed, with the opposite assertion: under exact-origin dedup the live path admits the replayed pre-credit high instead of folding it into the existing event. That is a rename with a successor arriving in this transition, which is what cause 'renamed' records, and the original declaration filed it as 'retired' beside nine genuinely retired rows from another module. The text there justified the choice against 'reclassified', which is the mirror-boundary cause, and never considered 'renamed'. Corrected here so the ledger states what happened; the predecessorDigest is unchanged, so this declaration describes the transition already applied and authorizes nothing further.

#750 S3's Unit A review found that two names promise a dedup collision their bodies no longer exercise, and both are renamed in place: same file, same seed, same assertions, new names. Under exact-origin dedup the pre-seeded event in each case names no origin and is governed by the legacy tuple index, while the tick under test writes an origin-bearing row governed by the origin index, so the two identities never meet and no dedup decision is reached. The docstrings already said so; only the names still promised otherwise. test_reset_to_zero_crash_recovery_reruns_pivots becomes test_reset_to_zero_confirm_reruns_pivots_and_clears_the_state, which is what it asserts: the confirming zero re-runs the idempotent pivots and clears the debounce state. test_weekly_pivots_run_when_event_row_already_committed becomes test_weekly_pivots_run_beside_an_earlier_committed_event, because the recovery tick now opens its own event beside the pre-committed one rather than being refused by it; the refused-insert half of that invariant is pinned by tests/test_exact_origin_credit_dedup.py::test_a5_the_pivots_run_on_the_credits_own_terms. Cause 'renamed' rather than 'retired': each successor arrives in this same transition, which is the claim that cause records, and no coverage leaves the estate.

#750 S3's Unit B review found that tests/test_active_segment_selection.py::test_cmd_diff_resolves_the_account_before_it_builds_the_interval asserted a source-text ordering — body.index("resolve_account_filter") < body.index("_diff_resolve_anchor") — which passes for a cmd_diff that resolves the account early and then still calls _diff_resolve_anchor with no account_key. That is the whole defect the name promises to guard, so the node is renamed in place to test_cmd_diff_threads_the_resolved_account_into_the_anchor, in the same file, and rewritten to spy on the call and assert the resolved account reaches it. Coverage grows rather than shrinks: the new node fails when the account_key argument is removed from the call, which the retired one did not, and that was verified by re-introducing exactly that defect and observing RED (assert None == 'acct-b').

#750 S2 bumped STATS_INDEX_EPOCH from 1011 to 1012 to add the four metering-rate disclosure columns to the stats index. test_live_ingest_acquires_maintenance_before_ingest_lock derives its parametrized ids from that constant, so the same two cases now enumerate as [0-1012] and [1012-1012]. The test body, its assertions and its coverage are unchanged and nothing left the estate; only the ids the parametrization computes moved with the epoch.

#750 S2 moved the alert toast's dismiss hint rather than dropping it, so these six cases moved from the '#700 — the head drops the dismiss hint exactly when it names an account' describe into '#749 — the dismiss hint moves out of the head instead of vanishing', which changed every id. Coverage did not leave the estate: all six scenarios are still asserted in the same file, and each gained assertions rather than losing any. Three of them — the decorated Claude threshold, Codex threshold and metering-rate cases — also had their expectation inverted, from asserting the hint is absent to asserting it renders on its own line below the alert body, because #749 is precisely the defect that the hint vanished exactly when an account label appeared. The three undecorated cases keep their behaviour and gained a position assertion.
